x: Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal published after independence. The other options describe other papers: Navasakthi was the first fully socialist Telugu journal, Desabhimani the only Telugu daily of British Andhra, and Satyadoota (Bellary, 1835) the first Telugu newspaper.

Mutnuri Krishna Rao made Krishna Patrika a political weekly and a hub for freedom fighters, which made it a centre of political awakening (1, 2 and 4). It was never a commercial banking journal, so 3 is wrong.

Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika (1908) and Bharati (1924). Krishna Patrika was founded in 1902 by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao, and Swarajya (1907) was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's paper. Hence 1 and 2 only.
All four statements are correct. Nageswara Rao (1867-1947) was titled Desoddharaka, and in the spirit of Gandhian trusteeship he used the wealth of his Amrutanjan business to fund his public work.

Vijnana Chandrika Mandali was founded by Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao at Hyderabad in 1905 (APHQ says 1906), not at Vijayawada. The other pairs are correct: Andhra Saraswati Parishad (Hyderabad, 1922), C.V.N. Granthalayam (Ongole, 1890), Andhra Council of Research (Kovvur, 1916).

Only a is correct: Dharma Granthalaya was Yatagiri Lakshmi Venkataramana's journal (Kakinada). Andhra Granthalayam was edited by P. Rajasekharam (A. Srinivasa Rao was its publisher; Suri Venkatasastri wrote pamphlets), Grandhalaya Sarvasvam was published by the ADLA, and Andhra Patrika was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's paper.

Only a is correct: Kotha Sivaramakrishnayya ran the boat library at Sangam Jagarlamudi. The library pilgrimage was Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya's, the Bank Canal boat library was Pathuri Nagabhushanam's, and the 1918 padava yatra was Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao's.
Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya received the title Granthalaya Pitamaha from the Maharaja of Baroda.

Paturi Nagabhushanam was called Andhra Desa Granthalayodyama Roopasilpi, the Architect of the Andhra Library Movement. Library Gandhi was Velaga Venkatappayya (not Ayyanki), and Andhra Charitra Pitamaha was Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao (not Gadicherla).

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Seventh Amendment abolished the Part A/B/C/D classification and replaced it with states and Union Territories. Statement 3 is wrong: it abolished, not retained, the office of Rajpramukh. Hence 1 and 2 only.
